messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Activation clearance: network sanity sprint & smoke staging

Hi Diego / ACME ops,

We’re on track for the private deployment activation window next Friday (2026-09-17). Before we schedule the final cutover, I want to run a short, focused "network sanity + smoke staging" exercise that validates the VPC peering, ACLs, NAT egress, and the KV-cache priming sequence with a minimal traffic profile. Goal is to exercise the happy-path and one fallback lane.

Proposed plan (90m):
- 10:00–10:15: ingress/egress connectivity verification (ping/traceroute, natted egress)
- 10:15–10:35: ACL rule verification + stateful session checks (simulate app session open/close)
- 10:35–11:00: KV cache priming + read/write smoke calls (low token counts)
- 11:00–11:30: failure injection: simulate backend worker eviction and verify fallback model variant routing
- 11:30–11:40: quick telemetry sanity and log bundle collection

Attached: VPC-runbook-v3.pdf (runbook), smoke-test-playbook.xlsx (step-level checks), network-acl-change.diff (proposed minor ACL tweak we discussed).

Questions/asks for ACME before we run:
1) Please confirm the CIDR ranges and egress NAT IPs we should validate against (I have the numbers from the last handoff but want a final confirmation).
2) Will your platform-ops team be available for the injection window? We expect a single SRE + one network engineer.
3) Any compliance hold points we should be aware of for log collection?

If you’re good, we’ll schedule this for 2026-09-10 10:00 PT (tomorrow) as a dry-run; we’ll treat it as a production-adjacent rehearsal and capture artifacts. Reply with availability and any edits to the checklist.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — quick status from our side.

We can run the dry-run tomorrow at 10:00 PT. Internal readiness:
- Runbook: VPC-runbook-v3 reviewed; I added explicit steps for the KV priming TTLs (see smoke-test-playbook.xlsx).
- Binaries/config: the deployment image and quantized artifacts are already staged in the ACME-controlled bucket (verify access during the run).
- Telemetry: I’ve got a preconfigured dashboard and a streaming slice for the smoke calls, will share the link after this thread.

Outstanding items (please action):
- Karthik: confirm the exact NAT egress IPs and whether ACME does 1:1 NAT or SNAT rewrite for the control-plane calls. We need the final IPs to lock firewall rules.
- Laura: can you confirm the ACL diff will not impact the management VLAN? We should avoid changes on the management path during this rehearsal.
- Diego / ACME: need a named point-of-contact for the 10:00–11:40 window (SRE + Network).

If we run tomorrow we’ll treat it as a rehearsal; if anything fails we’ll capture evidence and follow the rollback path in section 7.2 of the runbook.

—Monica

Quick note on the ACL patch:
- I reviewed network-acl-change.diff and it only opens a narrow TCP egress from the app-subnet to the telemetry collector on port 6514 and allows the redis-kv host pair to accept inbound from the edge fabric.
- Management VLAN is untouched — I explicitly added a guard to the diff to prevent accidental applies there.
- I will be on the bridge tomorrow and will run the change with a double-check (apply -> smoke probe -> revert if any unexpected packets are dropped).

One request: if ACME can provide the expected traceroute hop counts for their transit, it speeds troubleshooting.

Laura Bennett
Network Product Manager
Redwood Inference
